title: A Hubble-flow proxy needs timescape geometry and observer clocks

source_evidence.locator: Secs.4.4-7, Eq.(1), Tables1-2, AppendixA; PDF pp6-20

assumptions: A one-dimensional finite-infinity line fraction and its inferred radii are operational catalogue quantities, distinct from Buchert three-dimensional wall/void volume shares.
Dressed H uses wall proper time tau and a=abar/gamma, gamma=dt/dtau; H=gamma Hbar-dgamma/dt. A phenomenological linear line-fraction interpolation alone does not supply this relation.
The tested alternative retains Millennium LambdaCDM matter/velocity ancestry and imposes a deformation with b_soft=0.75; no full timescape catalogue prediction is supplied.
predictions: The Saulder observations favor their LambdaCDM mocks over their imposed differential-expansion proxy; Table2 binned discrepancies are reported1.52sigma(LG) and2.08sigma(CMB), conditional on that proxy and mock uncertainties.
Table1 strong significance claims are retained only as source-reported values with an unresolved displayed-sigma inconsistency; no raw-statistic repair is inferred.

A valid timescape approximation must predict both sightline fractions and relative Hubble observables under a declared curved geometry, lapse, selection and distance calibration; endpoint matching or enhanced coherent infall is insufficient.
The reply establishes a missing model-to-observable contract, not observational confirmation of timescape or a proof that every nonlinear proxy fails.
